QS.question: Explain five causes of inflation.
QS.solution: Strong consumption, credit or public spending can push demand above capacity. Wage increases exceeding productivity lift unit costs. Energy and raw-material shocks raise production costs. Depreciation can increase import prices. Supply disruptions and bottlenecks reduce available output. Expectations can amplify these pressures.

QS.question: Explain fiscal measures for controlling inflation.
QS.solution: Contractionary fiscal policy reduces demand by cutting or deferring government spending, reducing transfers, or raising net taxes. Higher taxes reduce disposable income and consumption, while lower public spending directly reduces aggregate demand. The appropriate mix depends on the source of inflation. Supply-side measures can relieve bottlenecks when costs drive the price increase.

NOTES.html:
The average and marginal cost test

Separate fixed and variable cost before dividing by output. TC = TFC + TVC, AC = AVC + AFC and MC = dTC/dQ. When MC is below an average it pulls that average down, and when it is above the average it pulls it up. If labour is the only variable input and w is fixed, AVC = w/AP and MC = w/MP.

NOTES.html:
Contribution, break-even, and safety margin

Each unit contributes selling price minus variable cost to fixed costs and profit. Break-even units = fixed cost/unit contribution. P/V = unit contribution ÷ price. Break-even revenue = fixed cost ÷ P/V. Profit = sales × P/V − fixed cost. Margin of safety is the gap above break-even. Round up only when the question asks for a feasible number of whole units.

Cash-flow timing and equivalence

Pick a single comparison date. Discount later amounts or compound earlier amounts to it. An ordinary annuity starts at the end of year 1. An arithmetic gradient component starts at zero in year 1 and reaches (n−1)G at year n. Use the actual effective rate for the cash-flow period, keeping percentages and decimals distinct.

Choosing a project appraisal method

PW discounts signed cash flows to year 0. FW compounds to the terminal year. AW converts PW into a level amount. Compare equal service or use a defensible common study period. NOTES.html:
Depreciation schedules

Keep opening book value, annual charge, accumulated depreciation and closing book value separate. Straight line allocates the depreciable amount equally. Sinking fund uses a fixed deposit, while annual depreciation includes interest earned on the previous fund balance. Declining balance applies a percentage to opening book value without crossing the salvage floor.

NOTES.html:
Inflation and stabilization tools

Demand-pull: AD shifts right when consumption, investment, public spending or exports surge. In a standard short-run model, price and output rise. Cost-push: a wage, energy, or import-cost shock shifts SRAS left. Price rises while real output falls.

The central bank influences credit and liquidity with policy rates, reserve requirements, and market operations. Fiscal measures change taxes and public expenditure. A contractionary demand policy can curb price pressure but may also slow output.
